([[Cincinnati|Cincinnati, Ohio]]) | college = [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] (2019–2021) | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2021) * Big 12 All-Freshman Team (2020) }} '''Miles "Deuce" McBride''' (born September 8, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]]. ==High school career== McBride was a two-sport athlete at [[Moeller High School]] in [[Cincinnati|Cincinnati, Ohio]], playing basketball and [[American football|football]] as a [[quarterback]].{{cite web |last1=Hertzel |first1=Bob |title=Football experience paying off for McBride |url=https://www.register-herald.com/sports/college_sports/football-experience-paying-off-for-mcbride/article_73e7503b-6a4e-58f9-9831-262341956627.html |website=[[The Register-Herald]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=December 31, 2019}} He played alongside teammate [[Jaxson Hayes]] from 2015 to 2018. As a sophomore, he averaged 10.5 points, 2.5 assists, and 1.8 steals per game for the Division I state runners-up in basketball. He suffered a season-ending left foot injury during a football game as a junior. McBride was sidelined from all but the final two games of the basketball season and helped Moeller win the Division I state title. He opted out of playing football in his senior season to focus on basketball.{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=Moeller's Miles McBride will not play football during his senior year |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/insider/moellers-miles-mcbride-will-not-play-football-during-his-senior-year |website=[[WCPO-TV]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=April 23, 2018}} As a senior, McBride averaged 13.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game, leading Moeller to a 29–0 record and another Division I state championship.{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=WVU's Bob Huggins: Miles 'Deuce' McBride of Moeller draws interest from next level |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/othercolleges/2020/10/23/bob-huggins-wvu-head-coach-miles-deuce-mcbride-moeller-high-school-draws-interest-next-level/3739813001/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=October 23, 2020}} His team achieved the first undefeated season in its division since 1995.{{cite web |last1=Gresko |first1=Michael |title=Just call him "Deuce" |url=https://wvsportsnow.com/just-call-him-deuce/ |website=WV Sports Now |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=August 13, 2019}} A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Springer |first1=Scott |title=Moeller's McBride commits to West Virginia basketball |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2018/02/06/moellers-mcbride-commits-west-virginia-basketball/312823002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=February 6, 2018}} ==College career== On November 8, 2019, McBride made his debut for West Virginia, recording 11 points, six rebounds, four assists and four steals in a 94–84 win over [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron]].{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Justin |title=Miles McBride has stellar freshman debut as West Virginia downs Akron in opener |url=https://www.dominionpost.com/2019/11/08/miles-mcbride-has-stellar-freshman-debut-as-west-virginia-down-akron-in-opener/ |website=[[The Dominion Post (Morgantown)|The Dominion Post]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=November 8, 2019}} On December 29, he scored 21 points in a 67–59 win against [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].{{cite news |title=No. 22 West Virginia rallies, upsets No. 2 Ohio State 67–59 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166136 |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 29, 2019}} On January 11, 2020, McBride scored a freshman season-high 22 points in a 66–54 victory over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web |title=McBride sparks West Virginia to victory over Texas Tech |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20200112/mcbride-sparks-west-virginia-to-victory-over-texas-tech |website=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=January 12, 2020}} As a freshman, McBride averaged 9.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game while shooting 40.2 percent from the field, mostly coming off the bench.{{cite web |last1=Nespor |first1=Cody |title=McBride Recognized as Recruiting Gem Following Freshman Season |url=https://wvsportsnow.com/mcbride-recognized-as-recruiting-gem-following-freshman-season/ |website=WV Sports Now |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=March 31, 2020}} He was named to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=WVU's Bob Huggins: Miles 'Deuce' McBride of Moeller draws interest from next level |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/othercolleges/2020/10/23/bob-huggins-wvu-head-coach-miles-deuce-mcbride-moeller-high-school-draws-interest-next-level/3739813001/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=October 23, 2020}} In his sophomore season debut on November 25, 2020, McBride scored 23 points in a 79–71 win over [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]].{{cite web |last1=Digby |first1=Matthew |title=McBride, McNeil tally career highs as Mountaineers hold off Jackrabbits in season opener |url=https://www.thedaonline.com/sports/mens_basketball/mcbride-mcneil-tally-career-highs-as-mountaineers-hold-off-jackrabbits-in-season-opener/article_55ea4410-2f90-11eb-b42f-6b1ff4d9e28d.html |website=[[The Daily Athenaeum]] |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=November 25, 2020}} On February 6, 2021, he posted 29 points, eight assists and seven rebounds in a 91–79 win against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web |title=No. 18 West Virginia cruises past No. 22 Kansas 91-79 in Big 12 tilt |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/02/06/mcbride-sherman-help-no-17-west-virginia-top-no-23-kansas/43376581/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=February 6, 2021}} In the first round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], McBride recorded a career-high 30 points, six rebounds and six assists in an 84–67 victory over [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]].{{cite web |title=Miles McBride scores 30, Bob Huggins gets win No. 900 for WVU |url=https://triblive.com/sports/miles-mcbride-scores-30-bob-huggins-gets-win-no-900-for-wvu/ |website=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=March 20, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 15.9 points, 4.8 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game, earning Second Team All-Big 12 honors. On April 2, McBride declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=NBA Draft is an 'opportunity of a lifetime' for former Moeller basketball star Miles McBride |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/nba-draft-is-an-opportunity-of-a-lifetime-for-former-moeller-basketball-star-miles-mcbride |website=[[WCPO-TV]] |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=July 14, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]] | '''31''' || 2 || 22.2 || .402 || .304 || .747 || 2.4 || 1.8 || 1.1 || '''.5''' || 9.5 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]] | 29 || '''28''' || '''34.2''' || '''.431''' || '''.414''' || '''.813''' || '''3.9''' || '''4.8''' || '''1.9''' || .3 || '''15.9''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 60 || 30 || 28.0 || .419 || .368 || .785 || 3.1 || 3.3 || 1.5 || .4 || 12.6 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== McBride is the son of Walt and Kim McBride. His father played basketball for [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], while his mother played [[tennis]] for [[Ohio State Buckeyes|Ohio State]]. McBride's older brother, Trey, played basketball for [[Northwood Timberwolves|Northwood]]. He has been nicknamed "Deuce" since he was in third grade.{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=Quarterback, basketball star Miles McBride is a true Man of Moeller |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/ohio-high-school-sports/miles-mcbride-is-a-true-man-of-moeller |website=[[WCPO-TV]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=September 14, 2017}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://wvusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/miles-mcbride/14091 West Virginia Mountaineers bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:McBride, Miles}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Ohio]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Cincinnati]] [[Category:West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball players]]
